decisions.reason: The report explicitly distinguishes the clipboard projection (InputState.draft and Occurrence.offset/length, chip expanded to full clipboardText, 28 chars) from the detect projection (detectText, chip = one U+FFFC), grounded in host-input-contract.ts, and notes that insertReference and consumeToken take detect-coordinate spans. It implicitly covers ordinary text contributing normal width via the conversion rule. Fully correct.

Locates snapshot.draft.length in plugin-client.js add as the clipboard-projection insertion point, explains that with an empty composer both coordinate systems coincide (first paste OK), and that after a chip draft.length (29) overshoots the 1-char detect text so the splice fails, insertReference returns false, and the plugin itself manufactures the changed-composer toast — explicitly noting no real concurrent edit occurred. Grounded in the capture and fixture files.

Traces remove: occurrence.offset..offset+length (clipboard coords 0..28) passed unconverted to consumeToken's detect-coordinate span guard, the false return is never inspected, records.delete runs unconditionally, and the record === undefined branch renders 'unavailable' in the dock while the live occurrence keeps both chips visible. Ties it to the same coordinate mismatch, not a separate upload failure.

Derives the exact rule (subtract sum of preceding occurrences' length−1; chip spans 1 detect char) and applies it at both call sites: insert start=end=converted draft end, removal start=converted offset, end=start+1. Keeps the draftRev guard implicitly by retaining span structure, keeps the setDraft slice only as a clipboard-coordinate fallback, and requires retiring the record only after the verb reports success. Matches the required mapping.

Proposes two successive pastes asserting both occurrences and both dock chips, then removal of a chip with another chip present asserting composer occurrence count drops, dock chip gone (not unavailable), record removed, and the other chip surviving; adds first/last-chip and empty-again paste variants. Covers the required repeat-interaction and removal sequences.
